cohort: This study included 332 young adult twins from the East Flanders Prospective Twin Survey (EFPTS) cohort.
finding: The built environment in which mothers resided during pregnancy, specifically early-life exposure to residential green spaces and distance to highway, was associated with body composition measurements such as waist-to-hip ratio, waist circumference, and body fat percentage in young adult twins, with differential effects observed based on zygosity/chorionicity type.
